# F0 spike — reference data for the 3D EM backends

Hand-written solver inputs and the outputs the solvers wrote, for the two cases of
`docs/sonnet-briefs/brief-em3d-1-f0-spike.md`. The findings — what these numbers answer — are in
`docs/design/em-3d-f0-findings.md`. Produced on 2026-09-24.

**Why this directory exists (overview §1h).** These are the *externally generated* references that
brief 7 (Palace) and brief 9 (openEMS) gate against. **Nothing here was produced by circuitRF's 3D
generator, and nothing here may be regenerated by it later.** The `.geo` scripts and Palace configs are
written by hand; the openEMS XML files were written by openEMS's own Python interface from the
hand-written scripts in `*/openems/source/`, which is the solver authors' own code and so a *better*
structural oracle than a hand-typed file. Those scripts are spike material: **nothing under `src/` or
`tools/` may import, copy or call them** (the GPL boundary, em-3d.md §5.2).

## Layout

```
A-bondwire/                       case A — one 1 mil gold bond wire over ground, 1–40 GHz, 40 points
    palace-round/                 case.geo  config.json  entities.txt  gmsh.log  palace.log  postpro/  reference.s2p
    palace-hex/                   perimeter-matched hexagon (side πd/6, flat bottom)
    palace-hex-foot/              the hexagon with a 2d wedge foot at each end
    palace-round-pec-wire/        the round wire as PEC — the lossless twin openEMS is compared with
    palace-round-amr/, palace-hex-amr/   the same with 2 AMR iterations (the mesh's own spread);
                                         postpro/iteration1 = initial mesh, iteration2, top level = final
    palace-round-order1/          Q6 control: void + boundary at element order 1, 1 GHz only
    palace-round-meshed-wire/     Q6: the wire meshed as a gold volume, order 1, 1 GHz only
    openems/source/               make_case.py (writes case.xml), postproc.py (probes -> S)
    openems/curve-dw25/           thin PEC curve on grid edges, 25 µm grid at the wire
    openems/wire-dw{12.7,6.35,4.2333,3.175}/   PEC wire of the true 12.7 µm radius — Q2's grid ladder
    kernelw/                      case.wBond, case.cnl; kernel W (distributed) at 24 and 96 segments,
                                  and the lumped wBond model (the netlist route)
B-via/                            case B — microstrip -> via -> inverted microstrip, 0.1–20 GHz, 200 points
    palace/                       copper voids with σ 5.8e7, tanδ 0.004
    palace-lossless/              the lossless twin (PEC copper, tanδ 0) — mesh of palace/
    palace-sheet-lines/           Q6: the lines as zero-thickness sheets with Thickness 35 µm
    openems/source/               make_case.py, postproc.py
    openems/dw25-lossless/        lossless, 25 µm grid; stopped by hand at 38.3 ns (see below)
    openems/dw25-lossy/           κ fitted at 10 GHz, PEC copper, 73,000 steps (2.0 ns)
    planar/ws, planar/ws-meshed-plane, planar/REFUSED.md   circuitRF planar MoM: refused, verbatim
tools/                            palace2s2p.py, summarize.py, spread.py, palace_metrics.py (spike material)
probes/q8-polyhedron/q8.py        Q8: does CSXCAD read an STL / PLY polyhedron
```

**`reference.s2p` in every run directory** is that run's result as a 2-port Touchstone (RI, 50 Ω),
converted by hand-checked arithmetic — `tools/palace2s2p.py` (Palace's dB/degree CSV to RI) or
`openems/source/postproc.py` (each probe file's own time column into a DFT; it agrees with openEMS's
own `CalcPort` to 1e-16 in every run). Each file's `!` header names the run. **Port 1 is the only port
excited in every run**, so S22 and S12 are filled from S11 and S21 by the geometry's symmetry — mirror
about x = 0 for case A, 180° rotation about the via axis for case B — and each header says so.
kernel W's files are its own export (all four parameters computed), except that its header's dashes
come out as `?`.

**Not committed:** meshes (`case.msh`, 2.6–13 MB each, regenerated by `gmsh case.geo -3 -o case.msh`,
deterministic for a given Gmsh), field dumps, openEMS's `et`/`ht` excitation traces, the kernel W
scratch harness (a ten-line console program calling `WBondTouchstoneExport.Export` with
`Model: Distributed` — kernel W has no CLI route), and the first two openEMS case B attempts killed at
14 and 10 minutes (their logs are summarised below). `postpro/palace.json` and `config_resolved.json` are
committed: timings and memory per phase, and the config with every default resolved.

## The two cases, as built

The brief fixes the physics; where it left a dimension open, this is what was chosen, **and the choice
is part of the reference** — a generated problem matches it only if it makes the same choice.

**Case A.** PEC box x [−1500, 1500] y [−1000, 1000] z [0, 1100] µm; its floor is the ground. Substrate
z [0, 100], εr 9.8, tanδ 0, the full footprint. Pads 100 × 100 µm, **zero-thickness PEC**, centred at
x = ±500 on the substrate. Ports: 100 µm-wide vertical sheets **at the pads' outer edges (x = ±550)**
from ground up to the pad, 50 Ω, both oriented +z. Wire: gold σ₂₀ = 4.10×10⁷ S/m at 20 °C, a **void**
with Palace's conductivity boundary; axis polyline (x, z above the substrate top) (−475, a),
(−325, a + 150), (325, a + 150), (475, a), with a half the section's height, so wBond's loop height
(max − min z of the axis) is **150 µm exactly**. The assembly-definition loop height (§6.6: pad top to
the wire's top surface at the apex) is 150 + 2a = **175.4 µm** round, **173.0 µm** hexagon. Without a foot
the end segments continue below the pad plane and the wire is cut there (flat contact face); with a foot
a 2d = 50.8 µm horizontal run lies on each pad outward from the end point. Joints are **mitred** (see
Q5). kernel W sees the same axis polyline (`kernelw/case.wBond`, `OperatingTempC` 20, air, ground
plane on) — no substrate, no pads, terminals at the wire ends.

**Case B.** Mirror-symmetric stack, z up: bottom copper [0, 35], dielectric [35, 235], ground plane
[235, 270], dielectric [270, 470], top copper [470, 505] µm; εr 3.66, tanδ 0.004; copper 5.8×10⁷ S/m.
Board x [−5000, 5000] y [−2500, 2500]; lines **400 µm wide** (50.4 Ω by Hammerstad–Jensen with
Wheeler's thickness correction), top line x [−5000, 0], bottom line x [0, 5000]; pads d 600, via
barrel d 300 (solid: only its outer surface carries RF current), antipad d 900 **filled with
dielectric**. Air 1500 µm beyond the board on every side; outer walls **first-order absorbing** (Palace
`Absorbing` order 1, openEMS `MUR`). Ports: sheets at the line ends from the plane to the line; port 1
+z, port 2 −z, so both voltages are line minus ground.

## Commands

Palace, from each run directory (the Spack environment loaded):

```
gmsh case.geo -3 -o case.msh                 # writes entities.txt beside it
palace -np 8 config.json                     # writes postpro/
python3 ../../tools/palace2s2p.py postpro/port-S.csv reference.s2p "<title>" "<symmetry sentence>"
```

openEMS, from `*/openems/` (openEMS's venv active):

```
python source/make_case.py curve-dw25 curve 25          # case A: <outdir> <curve|wire> <grid step µm>
python source/make_case.py wire-dw6.35 wire 6.35
python source/make_case.py dw25-lossless 25 lossless    # case B: <outdir> <step> [lossy|lossless] [max steps]
python source/make_case.py dw25-lossy 25 lossy 73000
cd <outdir> && openEMS case.xml && cd ..
python source/postproc.py <outdir> <outdir>/reference.s2p "<title>"
```

kernel W: `circuitrf sparam kernelw/case.cnl -o reference-lumped.s2p` for the lumped model; the
distributed model through `WBondTouchstoneExport.Export(design, new Options(StartHz: 1e9, StopHz: 40e9,
Points: 40, Model: WBondNetworkModel.Distributed, SegmentsPerWire: 24|96), path)`.

Planar MoM: `circuitrf em B-via/planar/ws/via/em/via.cem` (and the two variants) — refused, exit 1,
`planar/REFUSED.md`.

**Removing the failed attempt's 443 MB** took more than `spack gc`, which in a directory environment sees
only the environment's own specs, and outside it looks at the default store. The 24 dead builds were
uninstalled by hash from a plain Spack pointed at the environment's store (`spack -c
config:install_tree:root:… -c config:install_tree:padded_length:256 -c repos:local:<palace>/spack_repo/local
uninstall -y /<hash> …`; without the `repos:` entry it fails with `Unknown namespace: local`). **One
build in the dead tree was live**: `gmake`, which the working environment still uses as a build tool,
because its own `require:` line overrides the `all: target=m3` entry. An uninstaller that deletes a
failed build's directory wholesale would have broken the next rebuild. Afterwards the store is 455 MB
and Palace still answers `--version` and `--dry-run`.

The environment file that finally built (Palace's `docs/src/developer/spack/spack.yaml` at v0.18.1, with
the spec line and one `packages:` entry changed, and the compiler and externals `setup-macos.sh` added):

```yaml
spack:
  specs:
  - local.palace@git.v0.18.1=0.18.0+superlu-dist+sundials+slepc+libxsmm+gslib~arpack
  packages:
    all:
      require: target=m3            # F0: m4 -> -march=armv9.2-a+sme2 -> SVE -> SIGILL on an M4
    # … the rest exactly as Palace's file: gcc for c/cxx/fortran, petsc ~hdf5, openmpi@5:,
    # openblas, metis -fPIC, gmake -std=gnu17, mfem +exceptions
  # plus, via `spack -e . repo add --scope=env:<dir> <palace>/spack_repo/local`, Palace's own recipe,
  # with Spack's builtin mfem package symlinked into it (Palace's documented workaround for
  # spack/spack#51505)
```
